questions.q: What is the matching principle in Duhigg's book?
a: Recognizing the kind of conversation and matching the other person
Repeating another person's words back to them exactly
Agreeing with whatever the other person says
Copying another person's gestures and posture
questions.why: Lesson 1 says effective communication means identifying the conversation type and then matching each other.

questions.q: Why did the shop owner's anger calm the complaining customer?
a: He got angry on her behalf, so only one of them stayed angry
He offered her a full refund on the spot
He stayed completely calm and said nothing
He blamed the manufacturer for the faulty button
questions.why: Lesson 1 tells the fur coat story, where shared anger let the customer shift to solving the problem.

questions.q: What mindset does a 'What's this really about?' conversation require?
a: A decision-making mindset
An emotional mindset
A social mindset
A competitive mindset
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes this conversation as logical and analytical, aimed at reaching a conclusion together.

questions.q: What should you do in a 'How do we feel?' conversation?
a: Listen for what is unsaid and show that you are listening
Push quickly toward a practical conclusion
Establish everyone's role within the group
Change the subject when things get heavy
questions.why: Lesson 2 says these conversations call for matching moods, deep questions and visible listening.

questions.q: What does Duhigg say you should do with your goals in a learning conversation?
a: Share them and ask the other person for theirs
Keep them private until the other person asks
State them only after agreement has been reached
Set them aside and adopt the other person's goals
questions.why: Lesson 3 lists sharing your goals and asking others for theirs as the second rule.
